findings.failure_path: Source discovery is required only when no visual-system source is found. An author can cite an inspected palette-only token contract, record its silence on containers, and classify library-default cards as design-freedom without inspecting a separate visual-direction document that forbids cards. The visual entry and treatment rows then satisfy the pre-edit gate while preserving the original failure class.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the relevant visual-source lookup before declaring a treatment unspecified, even when a token/component source was found. Add a regression scenario containing both a silent token contract and an authoritative visual-direction document.

findings.failure_path: Deleting the oracle's source-artifact fallback and 'at the same runtime and size' leaves every substring checked by the new validators intact. None of the added mutations targets these obligations, so the checks cannot detect their removal despite the acceptance requirement to protect each new obligation.
findings.smallest_fix: Assert the no-reference-surface fallback and matching runtime/size requirement, and add separate deletion mutations that fail the validator.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the frozen packet contains the raised constant but no consuming read/hash functions, aggregate accounting, or boundary tests. It therefore cannot establish that 1–4 MiB files reach reviewer selection while oversized files/packages remain rejected, or that reviewer egress remains bounded. The reported wrapper success does not independently establish those properties.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply frozen enforcement excerpts and candidate-bound test evidence for permitted reads, per-file and aggregate rejection, unchanged packet bounds, and real-controller reviewer selection.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The direct behavior-only brief path is blocked, but choosing a partial visual source still permits library-default treatments. The added validators also leave comparison obligations unprotected.
The constants show the intended limits, but the packet lacks consuming code and boundary-test evidence needed to verify enforcement and reviewer selection.
